```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(csgjcr)
library(highcharter)
library(htmlwidgets)
library(reactable)
library(reactablefmtr)

source("R/utils.R")
source("R/page-data.R")
source("R/local-map-data.R")

# htmlwidgets seeds its element IDs from this, so rerenders give identical HTML
set.seed(2019)

# params exists when Quarto renders; interactive runs use the YAML default
if (!exists("params")) {
  params <- list(state = "NY")
}

state <- csg_state_convert(params$state, from = "abbr", "name")
state_abbr_params <- params$state
state_name_text <- if_else(params$state == "DC", "the District of Columbia", state)
show_solved <- !state %in% states_to_exclude_from_solved_rate_viz

srs_state_new <- read_srs_state()
latest_year <- max(srs_state_new$year)
first_year <- latest_year - 10

srs_state <- violent_by_offense(srs_state_new, first_year, state)
srs_by_cat_state <- violent_totals(srs_state_new, first_year, state)
srs_by_cat_us <- violent_totals(srs_state_new, first_year)
srs_us <- violent_by_offense(srs_state_new, first_year)

### county map and agency tables come from R/01-prep-agency-county-data.R
srs_solved_by_county_to_map <- read_rds("data/county_map.rds") |>
  filter(state_abbr == state_abbr_params)

agency_table_all <- read_rds("data/agency_table.rds")

### years are read before filtering so states with no agency rows still get them
### the agency base year comes from the data built by R/01-prep-agency-county-data.R
agency_year <- agency_table_all$agency_year[1]
agency_base_year <- agency_table_all$base_year[1]

srs_solved_by_agency_to_table <- agency_table_all |>
  filter(state_abbr == state_abbr_params)

srs_solved_by_agency_and_offense_to_table <- read_rds("data/agency_offense_table.rds") |>
  filter(state_abbr == state_abbr_params)

### pages without solve-rate data drop "and arrests" from the title
doc_title <- if_else(
  show_solved,
  paste(state, "data on violent crime and arrests"),
  paste(state, "data on violent crime")
)
```

```{r }
### inflation-adjusted state and local police protection expenditures
asslgf_clean <- read_police_spending(state_abbr_params, read_inflation_index())

### officers per violent crime use each geography's SRS violent crime rate
lee_state <- read_lee_officers(c(state_abbr_params, "US")) |>
  mutate(state_name = if_else(geo_abbr == "US", "United States", state),
         state_abbr = geo_abbr)

ucr_employee_data_by_state_clean <- lee_state |>
  filter(geo_abbr == state_abbr_params) |>
  left_join(srs_by_cat_state |> select(year, violent_rate = incidents_reported_rate_total), by = "year") |>
  add_officer_rates()

ucr_employee_data_national_clean <- lee_state |>
  filter(geo_abbr == "US") |>
  left_join(srs_by_cat_us |> select(year, violent_rate = incidents_reported_rate_total), by = "year") |>
  add_officer_rates()
```

```{r }
### other states in this state's CSG region, for the homicide comparisons
csg_regions <- read_csv("data/csg-regions.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(state_abbr = csg_state_convert(state_name, "name", "abbr"))

csg_region <- csg_regions$csg_region[csg_regions$state_abbr == state_abbr_params]
csg_region_full <- paste0("CSG ", csg_region, " Region")

### homicide case characteristics from state-level SHR data
shr_state <- read_rds(csg_sp_path("jr_data_library", "data", "analysis", "fbi", "shr", "fbi_shr_state.rds"))
shr_years <- paste0(shr_first_year, "–", max(shr_state$year))
shr_region_abbr <- csg_regions$state_abbr[csg_regions$csg_region == csg_region &
                                            csg_regions$state_abbr != state_abbr_params]
shr_region_label <- paste0("Other ", csg_region, " States")
```

title: "`r doc_title`"
---

```{r}
min_max_viol_crime <- srs_by_cat_state |> 
  filter(year %in% range(year)) |> 
  arrange(year)

max_year <- min_max_viol_crime$year[2]
min_year <- min_max_viol_crime$year[1] 

pct_change_crime <- (min_max_viol_crime$incidents_reported_rate_total[2] - min_max_viol_crime$incidents_reported_rate_total[1]) / min_max_viol_crime$incidents_reported_rate_total[1]

change_text_crime <- change_phrase(pct_change_crime)

us_latest_rate <- srs_by_cat_us$incidents_reported_rate_total[srs_by_cat_us$year == latest_year]
us_state_rate_comp <- (min_max_viol_crime$incidents_reported_rate_total[2] - us_latest_rate) / us_latest_rate
us_state_rate_text_crime <- change_phrase(us_state_rate_comp)

pct_change_solved <- min_max_viol_crime$pct_solved[2] - min_max_viol_crime$pct_solved[1]
change_text_clear <- change_phrase(pct_change_solved, "point")
```

## Violent crime in `r state_name_text`

```{r}
crime_rate_max <- paste0(comma(min_max_viol_crime$incidents_reported_rate_total[2], 1, scale = 1e5))
```

In `r max_year`, `r crime_rate_max` violent crime incidents per 100,000 residents were reported to police in `r state_name_text`. This is `r change_text_crime` the violent crime rate in `r min_year`.

The crime rate in `r state_name_text` in `r latest_year` was `r us_state_rate_text_crime` the United States average.

Data regarding crime and solve rates come from the FBI's [Uniform Crime Reporting Program](https://www.fbi.gov/how-we-can-help-you/need-an-fbi-service-or-more-information/ucr). Violent crime includes homicide, aggravated assault, robbery, and rape. Crime rates are calculated by dividing the number of estimated incidents by the total population for a given geography. For more information, see the data sources and methodology section below.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## All violent crime

```{r}
violent_rates <- srs_by_cat_state |>
  bind_rows(srs_by_cat_us) |>
  mutate(
    incidents_reported_rate_total = incidents_reported_rate_total * 1e5,
    tooltip = paste0(
      "<b>", state_name, " – ", year, "</b><br>",
      "Violent incidents per 100k: ", comma(incidents_reported_rate_total, 1), "<br>",
      "Violent incidents reported: ", comma(incidents_reported, 1)
    )
  )

trend_chart(
  violent_rates, "incidents_reported_rate_total",
  paste0("Violent crime in ", state_name_text),
  "Crime reported to police per 100,000 residents",
  "FBI UCR Program, state crime estimates",
  value_label = "violent incidents per 100,000 residents",
  compare = TRUE, expansion = axis_expansion_mult
)
```

```{r}
offense_rates <- srs_state |>
  bind_rows(srs_us) |>
  left_join(offense_pal, by = c("group" = "crime")) |>
  group_by(year, state_abbr) |>
  mutate(
    tot_crime = sum(incidents_reported),
    pct = incidents_reported / tot_crime,
    incidents_reported_rate_total = incidents_reported_rate_total * 1e5
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    group = fct_reorder(group, incidents_reported_rate_total),
    tooltip = paste0(
      "<b>", state_name, " – ", group, " – ", year, "</b></br>",
      "Incidents reported per 100k: ", comma(incidents_reported_rate_total, 1), "<br>",
      "Incidents reported: ", comma(incidents_reported, 1), "<br>",
      "Total violent incidents reported: ", comma(tot_crime, 1), "<br>",
      "Share of all violent incidents: ", percent(pct, 1)
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(year, group)

offense_color <- function(offense) offense_pal$color[offense_pal$crime == offense]
```

```{r}
offense_trend_chart(

)
```

## By offense

```{r}
state_offense_rates <- filter(offense_rates, state_name == state)

state_offense_rates |>
  hchart(
    "column",
    stacking = "normal",
    groupPadding = 0.05,
    hcaes(year, incidents_reported_rate_total, group = group),
    accessibility = list(point = list(
      valueDescriptionFormat = "{point.series.name}, year: {point.x:.0f}, incidents per 100,000 residents: {point.y:.1f}"
    ))
  ) |>
  hc_colors(unique(offense_rates$color)) |>
  hc_title(text = paste0("Violent crime in ", state_name_text, ", by offense")) |>
  hc_subtitle(text = "Crime reported to police per 100,000 residents") |>
  hc_caption(text = "FBI UCR Program, state crime estimates") |>
  hc_legend(reversed = "true") |>
  hc_setup()
```

```{r, eval=!state %in% states_to_exclude_from_solved_rate_viz}

### create state-specific labels for text output
solved_rate_max <- paste0(comma(min_max_viol_crime$pct_solved[2] * 100, 1), " percent")

### state averages pool every full-reporting agency in the state,
### including statewide and tribal agencies that are off the map
agency_state_rates <- srs_solved_by_agency_and_offense_to_table |>
  summarize(across(c(starts_with("n_reported_") & !starts_with("n_reported_rate"),
                     starts_with("n_solved_")), \(x) sum(x, na.rm = TRUE)))

agency_state_solve_share <- function(offense) {
  agency_state_rates[[paste0("n_solved_", offense)]] /
    agency_state_rates[[paste0("n_reported_", offense)]]
}

agency_state_solve_rate <- function(offense) {
  scales::comma(agency_state_solve_share(offense) * 100, 1)
}

state_average_agg_assault_solve_rate <- agency_state_solve_rate("aggravated_assault")

state_average_homicide_solve_rate <- agency_state_solve_rate("homicide")

state_average_rape_solve_rate <- agency_state_solve_rate("rape")

```

```{r, eval=!state %in% states_to_exclude_from_solved_rate_viz}
### rates below zero plot at zero and say so in the tooltip
violent_solve_rates <- srs_by_cat_state |>
  bind_rows(srs_by_cat_us) |>
  filter(year != solve_rate_skip_year) |>
  mutate(
    pct_solved_clean = ifelse(pct_solved < 0 & !is.na(pct_solved), 0, pct_solved) * 100,
    pct_solved_tooltip = ifelse(pct_solved < 0 & !is.na(pct_solved),
                                "Less than 0%", as.character(percent(pct_solved_clean / 100, 1))),
    incidents_solved_tooltip = ifelse(incidents_solved < 0 & !is.na(incidents_solved),
                                      "Fewer than 0", as.character(comma(incidents_solved))),
    tooltip = paste0(
      "<b>", state_name, " – ", year, "</b><br>",
      "Solve rate: ", pct_solved_tooltip, "<br>",
      "Violent incidents reported: ", comma(incidents_reported, 1), "<br>",
      "Violent incidents solved: ", incidents_solved_tooltip
    )
  )

trend_chart(
  violent_solve_rates, "pct_solved_clean",
  paste("Violent crime solve rate in ", state_name_text),
  caption = "FBI UCR Program, state crime estimates and clearances",
  value_label = "solve rate", value_format = "{point.y:.1f}%",
  compare = TRUE, expansion = axis_expansion_mult, y_format = "{value:,.0f}%"
)
```

```{r, eval=!state %in% states_to_exclude_from_solved_rate_viz}
offense_solve_rates <- srs_state |>
  filter(year != solve_rate_skip_year) |>
  left_join(offense_pal, by = c("group" = "crime")) |>
  mutate(
    pct_solved_clean = ifelse(pct_solved < 0 & !is.na(pct_solved), 0, pct_solved) * 100,
    pct_solved_tooltip = ifelse(pct_solved < 0 & !is.na(pct_solved),
                                "Less than 0%", as.character(percent(pct_solved_clean / 100, 1))),
    incidents_solved_tooltip = ifelse(incidents_solved < 0 & !is.na(incidents_solved),
                                      "Fewer than 0", as.character(comma(round(incidents_solved, digits = 0))))
  ) |>
  mutate(
    group = fct_reorder(group, pct_solved, last),
    tooltip = paste0(
      "<b>", group, " – ", year, "</b></br>",
      "Solve rate: ", pct_solved_tooltip, "<br>",
      "Incidents reported: ", comma(incidents_reported, 1), "<br>",
      "Incidents solved: ", incidents_solved_tooltip
      )
    ) |> 
  arrange(desc(year), pct_solved_clean)

offense_solve_rates |>
  hchart(
    "spline",
    hcaes(year, pct_solved_clean, group = group),
    accessibility = list(point = list(
      valueDescriptionFormat = "{point.series.name}, year: {point.x:.0f}, solve rate: {point.y:.1f}%"
    ))
  ) |>
  hc_colors(unique(offense_solve_rates$color)) |>
  hc_title(text = paste0("Violent crime solve rate in ", state_name_text, ", by offense")) |>
  hc_caption(text = "FBI UCR Program, state crime estimates and clearances") |>
  hc_setup() |>
  hc_yAxis(
    min = 0,
    max = max(100, ceiling(max(offense_solve_rates$pct_solved_clean, na.rm = TRUE) / 10) * 10),
    endOnTick = FALSE,
    labels = list(format = "{value:,.0f}%")
  )
```

```{r, eval=!state %in% states_to_exclude_from_solved_rate_viz}
#| fig-height: 5.5

### one row per map feature, so counties with no data still get a tooltip
map_name <- paste0("countries/us/us-", tolower(state_abbr_params), "-all")

srs_solved_by_county_to_map_tooltip <- local_county_features(map_name) |>
  left_join(srs_solved_by_county_to_map, by = "county_fips") |>
  ### counties with fewer than 25 reported incidents are grayed out on the map
  mutate(solved_rate_map = ifelse(n_reported < 25, NA, solved_rate)) |>
  ### convert solve rate from decimal to whole number -- for map legend
  mutate(solved_rate_map = solved_rate_map * 100) |>
  mutate(tooltip = case_when(
    n_reported >= 25 & !is.na(n_reported) ~ paste0(
      "<b>", county_label, " – ", agency_year, "</b><br>",
      "Solve rate: ", comma(solved_rate_map, 1), "%", "<br>",
      "Violent incidents reported: ", comma(n_reported, 1), "<br>",
      "Violent incidents solved: ", comma(n_solved, 1), "<br>",
      "Agencies reporting data: ", comma(n_agencies, 1), "<br>",
      "Population covered by reporting agencies: ", comma(pop_covered, 1), "<br>"
      ),
    n_reported < 25 & !is.na(n_reported) ~ paste0(
      "Agencies in ", county_label, " did not report enough", "<br>",
      "data on solved crime to the FBI to", "<br>",
      "make reliable estimates (fewer than 25 incidents)."
      ),
    is.na(n_reported) ~ paste0(
      "No agencies in ", county_label, " reported data", "<br>",
      "on solved crime to the FBI."
      )
    )
  )

### pull only state geo that we want for each param iteration
hcmap_local(
  map_name,
  data = srs_solved_by_county_to_map_tooltip,
  value = "solved_rate_map",
  joinBy = c("fips", "county_fips"),
  nullColor = "#E8E8E8",
  nullInteraction = TRUE,
  borderWidth = 0.45,
  borderColor = "black",
  accessibility = list(
      point = list(
        valueDescriptionFormat = "county: {point.county_label}, solve rate: {point.value:.1f}"
        )
      )) |> 
  hc_title(
    text = paste("Violent crime solve rate,", agency_year),
    align = "left",
    style = list(fontFamily = header_font, color = "#005FAD",
                              fontSize = "24px", fontWeight = "bold")
    ) |>   
  hc_colorAxis(endOnTick = TRUE,
               startOnTick = TRUE,
               stops = color_stops(length(rate_colors), rate_colors),
               labels = list(format = "{value:.0f}%",
                             style = list(fontSize = "12px",
                                          fontFamily = default_fonts))) |> 
  hc_legend(align = "center",
            horizontalAlign = "bottom",
            layout = "horizontal",
            symbolHeight = 25,
            symbolWidth = 315,
            x = 0,
            y = 0
            ) |> 
     hc_tooltip(
        style = list(fontFamily = default_fonts),
        formatter = JS("function() {
        return '<div style=\"background-color: #FFFFFF; opacity: 1; padding: 8px; border: none;\">' +
        this.point.tooltip +
        '</div>';}"),
        useHTML = TRUE
      ) |>
  hc_setup()

```

```{r, eval=!state %in% states_to_exclude_from_solved_rate_viz}
#| column: body-outset

### each agency is compared with the pooled state solve rate for the offense
offenses <- c("aggravated_assault", "homicide", "rape", "robbery")
state_solved_rate <- set_names(map_dbl(offenses, agency_state_solve_share), offenses)

solve_rate_layout <- list(
  aggravated_assault = list(offense = "Aggravated Assault", min_width = 100),
  homicide = list(offense = "Homicide", min_width = 100, align = "center"),
  rape = list(offense = "Rape", min_width = 100, align = "left"),
  robbery = list(offense = "Robbery", min_width = 100)
)

srs_solved_by_agency_and_offense_to_table |>
  filter(population > 0) |>
  select(
    agency_name, county, population,
    n_reported_rate_aggravated_assault, solved_rate_aggravated_assault,
    n_reported_rate_homicide, solved_rate_homicide,
    n_reported_rate_rape, solved_rate_rape,
    n_reported_rate_robbery, solved_rate_robbery
  ) |>
  mutate(across(starts_with("solved_rate_"), \(x) replace(x, is.nan(x), NA))) |>
  reactable_template(
    sort_col = list("population" = "desc"),
    columns = c(
      list(
        ### a right border sets off the sticky column
        agency_name = colDef(
          name = "Agency", minWidth = 200, sticky = "left",
          style = list(borderRight = "1px solid #eee"),
          headerStyle = list(borderRight = "1px solid #eee")
        ),
        county = colDef(name = "County", minWidth = 108),
```

```{r}
### years and inflation-adjusted percent change for spending text
max_year_resources <- max(asslgf_clean$year)
min_year_resources <- min(asslgf_clean$year)

pct_change_spending <- pct_change_first_last(asslgf_clean$n_inflation_adjusted_latest_year_dollars, asslgf_clean$year)

### years and percent change for officers per violent crime text
max_year_resources_staff_per_offense <- max(ucr_employee_data_by_state_clean$year)
min_year_resources_staff_per_offense <- min(ucr_employee_data_by_state_clean$year)

pct_change_staffing_per_violent_offense <- pct_change_first_last(
  ucr_employee_data_by_state_clean$officer_per_violent_offense_1k,
  ucr_employee_data_by_state_clean$year
)

### the cause sentence is skipped when the rate stayed about the same
### its last phrase is reversed because fewer crimes raise officers per crime
staffing_cause_text <- if (is_about_same(pct_change_staffing_per_violent_offense)) {
  ""
} else {
  paste0(
    " This ", change_direction(pct_change_staffing_per_violent_offense, "increase", "decrease"),
    " may be due to a combination of ",
    change_direction(pct_change_staffing_per_violent_offense, "an increase", "a decrease"),
    " in law enforcement officers and/or ",
    change_direction(pct_change_staffing_per_violent_offense, "a decrease", "an increase"),
    " in reported violent crimes."
  )
}

```

```{r, results='asis'}
Law enforcement resources also refer to the state’s staffing per 10,000 residents and per 1,000 violent crimes. These factors may show the level of policing a community receives, potentially influencing both crime and solve rates."))
```

::: {.callout-note icon=false collapse=true}

## Data sources and methodology

Data regarding crime and solve rates come from the FBI's [Uniform Crime Reporting Program](https://www.fbi.gov/how-we-can-help-you/need-an-fbi-service-or-more-information/ucr){target="_parent"}. Statewide counts of reported violent crime between `r first_year` and `r latest_year` are derived from the Summary Reporting System (SRS) and the National Incident-Based Reporting System (NIBRS). The FBI estimates reported crime for each state from agency-level reports, accounting for agencies that did not report, and publishes these estimates on its [Crime Data Explorer](https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST/webapp/#/pages/downloads){target="_parent"}. Statewide solve rates apply each state's clearance rate among agencies that reported to the FBI to the FBI's state estimates of reported crime. The county and agency sections use agency-level Summary Reporting System data from the Crime Data Explorer for `r agency_year`.

The FBI stopped SRS data collection after data year 2020 and required law enforcement agencies to use NIBRS to report crime statistics to the FBI. This change decreased the number of agencies that submitted their crime data and thus reduced the reliability of state estimates in 2021. The FBI later allowed agencies unable to submit NIBRS data to submit SRS data again. Comparisons involving 2021 should be interpreted with caution.

Statewide crime rates are calculated by dividing the number of estimated incidents by the total population of the state. Population data come from the U.S. Census Bureau [Population Estimates Program](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/popest.html){target="_parent"}.

Solve rates are the number of reported crimes cleared by arrest or by exceptional means divided by the number of reported crimes. A reported crime incident is [cleared by exceptional means](https://ucr.fbi.gov/crime-in-the-u.s/2019/crime-in-the-u.s.-2019/topic-pages/clearances){target='_parent'} if a law enforcement agency is unable to arrest or formally charge a person with a crime, but the agency has met the following conditions:
    
a) Identified the person who committed the crime
b) Gathered enough evidence to support an arrest, make a charge, and turn over the person to the court for prosecution
c) Identified the suspect’s exact location so that the person could be taken into custody immediately
d) Encountered a circumstance outside the control of law enforcement that prohibits the agency from arresting, charging, and prosecuting the person
    
Examples of exceptional clearances include the death of the person who committed the crime; the victim’s refusal to cooperate with the prosecution after the person who committed the crime has been identified; or the denial of extradition.

Annual clearances can exceed newly reported incidents because cases reported in earlier years may be cleared. As a result, annual solve rates can exceed 100 percent. The charts display rates below zero at zero and identify those values in their tooltips.

Agency- and county-level violent crime and solve rate data presented above are restricted to agencies reporting data for all 12 months in `r agency_year`. The calculation of population covered by reporting agencies, as well as the number of reporting agencies by county, is also based on agencies with violent crime data for all 12 months. 

Each law enforcement agency appears on the map in exactly one county. Agencies based in a single county use that county. Agencies whose jurisdiction spans several counties use the county holding the largest share of the agency's place or county subdivision population in the Census Bureau's 2025 Population Estimates, or the largest listed county when no place matches. The agency tables list every county an agency covers. Statewide and tribal agencies, along with a few agencies with no county, appear in the tables and in state totals but not on the map. In New York, the New York City Police Department and other agencies based in the five boroughs are combined into a single New York City area on the map. The population covered by reporting agencies is the sum of the jurisdiction populations of agencies reporting data for all 12 months in `r agency_year`. The change in solve rate since `r agency_base_year` compares each agency with itself and appears only for agencies that reported all 12 months in both years.

Counties with fewer than 25 reported violent incidents in `r agency_year` are excluded from the map, as calculations of solve rates are not reliable. 

Data regarding state and local police protection expenditures were downloaded from the U.S. Census Bureau [Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/gov-finances.html){target="_parent"}. Expenditures are adjusted to `r max_year_resources` dollars using the Chained Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers.

Officer employment analysis is restricted to sworn officers in state and local law enforcement agencies and uses the FBI's [Crime Data Explorer law enforcement employee data](https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST/webapp/#/pages/downloads){target="_parent"}. Officers per capita use the population served by agencies that reported employee counts. Officers per violent crime divide that rate by the state violent crime rate from the FBI state estimates.

Data on homicide solve rates and case characteristics come from the FBI's [Supplementary Homicide Reports](https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST/webapp/#/pages/downloads){target="_parent"}. Solve rates combine data from `r shr_first_year` through `r max(shr_state$year)`. Data from 2021 are excluded because many large states did not report SHR data during the transition to NIBRS.

:::
